rounds.text: G G Engineering Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic accounting value, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.32x [E1]. This deep valuation gap suggests the market has heavily discounted the company despite a long-term track record of substantial top-line expansion, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 42% over the last decade and 43% over the last five years [E7, E8]. While recent performance has faced headwinds, the company’s ability to sustain 19% compounded sales growth over the last three years demonstrates a proven capacity for scaling operations [E9]. Conceded: [E3, E5, E6, E10, E52, E53]. The current market capitalisation of ₹ 74.5 Cr remains modest relative to this historical growth trajectory [E2]. Investors are currently pricing the stock near the bottom of its 52-week range, potentially overlooking the underlying asset base that supports the current book value [E1, E4].

The bull’s reliance on a 0.32x price-to-book ratio [E1] ignores that assets are only as valuable as their ability to generate returns, and with an ROE of -0.2% and ROCE of 0.4%, the company is currently destroying shareholder value rather than preserving it [E5, E6]. While the bull highlights long-term sales growth [E7, E8], this historical data is rendered irrelevant by the most recent evidence showing a -7% decline in trailing twelve-month sales and a -39% year-over-year collapse [E10, E52]. The deceleration in earnings growth [E53] and the fact that price growth is currently running 96% ahead of profit delivery [E41] suggest that the market is not "overlooking" value, but rather pricing in a fundamental deterioration of the business model. Conceded: [E7, E8, E9]. The lack of any dividend yield [E3] further confirms that the company is failing to return capital to investors, leaving them with no tangible benefit while waiting for a turnaround that the recent negative growth trends actively contradict [E10, E52].

Compounded sales growth over 3 years is 19%.

PRICE-LED — Recently, price growth exceeds profit growth by 96% — expectations running ahead of delivery.
